description: How genes, proteins and metabolites interact as networks, and how those networks are analysed as graphs and simulated as differential-equation, stochastic, Boolean and constraint-based models. In the lab students build small gene circuits, run simulations, optimise metabolic fluxes and fit models to data.
modelledOn: Alon, An Introduction to Systems Biology: Design Principles of Biological Circuits
Klipp, Liebermeister, Wierling and Kowald, Systems Biology: A Textbook
Palsson, Systems Biology: Constraint-based Reconstruction and Analysis
Barabasi and Oltvai, Network Biology: Understanding the Cell's Functional Organization
outcomes: Represent gene regulatory, protein interaction and metabolic systems as graphs and compute their topological properties.
Build and simulate ordinary differential equation models of gene circuits and classify their steady states and oscillations.
Simulate stochastic cellular processes and explain when noise changes the behaviour predicted by a deterministic model.
Apply flux balance analysis to predict growth and the effect of gene knockouts in a metabolic network.
Build and analyse Boolean models of signalling and identify their attractors.
Fit model parameters to data and judge how well the data constrain them.

units.title: Networks inside the cell
topics: From genes to systems: levels of abstraction and the central dogma as a network
Gene regulatory networks: transcription factors, promoters and regulatory interactions
Protein-protein interaction networks: experimental methods, databases and false positives
Metabolic and signalling networks: pathways, enzymes and cascades
Graph representations: adjacency matrices, directed, signed, weighted and bipartite graphs
Network motifs: negative autoregulation, the feed-forward loop and what each does

units.title: Network topology and centrality
topics: Degree distributions: random, scale-free and hub-dominated networks
Clustering coefficient, path length and the small-world property
Centrality: degree, closeness, betweenness and eigenvector measures
Modules and community detection in interaction networks
Robustness and essentiality: hubs, bottlenecks and the centrality-lethality idea

units.title: Deterministic models of gene circuits
topics: Mass-action kinetics and ordinary differential equation models
Michaelis-Menten and Hill kinetics; cooperativity and ultrasensitivity
Production and degradation: steady state and response time of gene expression
The genetic toggle switch: bistability and hysteresis
The repressilator and negative-feedback oscillators
Phase planes, fixed points, stability analysis and bifurcations

units.title: Stochastic models of cellular processes
topics: Intrinsic and extrinsic noise in gene expression
The chemical master equation and its moments
The stochastic simulation algorithm (direct method)
Bursty gene expression, the Fano factor and noise-induced switching
Tau-leaping and when a deterministic model is good enough

units.title: Metabolic models and flux balance analysis
topics: Stoichiometric matrices and the steady-state condition S v = 0
Flux balance analysis as a linear program
Biomass objectives, growth prediction and gene knockout analysis
Flux variability analysis and genome-scale reconstructions
Exchange fluxes, media composition and a worked example of producing a biofuel or food additive from local feedstock

units.title: Boolean and logic models of signalling
topics: Boolean networks: states, update functions and truth tables
Synchronous versus asynchronous updating
Attractors, basins of attraction and cell fates
Logic models of signalling pathways built from literature
Perturbation analysis and drug-target prediction in logic models

units.title: Model fitting and parameter estimation
topics: Least-squares fitting of ODE models to time-course data
Identifiability and sloppy parameter sets
Local and global sensitivity analysis
Optimisation methods: gradient descent, simplex search and global search
Uncertainty and model selection: bootstrap, AIC and BIC
A first look at Bayesian parameter estimation with sampling

units.title: Building, sharing and applying models
topics: The modelling workflow from question to validated model, and SBML for exchange
Reproducible modelling: versioned models, units and annotations
Case study: host-pathogen networks in malaria and candidate drug targets
Mini project: build, simulate and fit a model of a small network

schedule.title: Biological networks and their data
schedule.exercise: Draw the lac operon as a regulatory network with signed edges, and list two reasons a high-throughput interaction map contains false positives.

tasks.title: Draw a regulatory network of 8 genes from a given table of transcription factor targets and list each gene's regulators
Load a 200-edge protein interaction table, build the graph, remove edges below a confidence cut-off, and report how the number of connected components changes
Compare a high-throughput interaction list with a curated reference set, compute precision and recall, and estimate the false-positive rate

schedule.title: Graph representations and network motifs
schedule.exercise: Write the adjacency matrix of a signed 5-gene network, trace a path through a signalling cascade, and sketch the response of a coherent feed-forward loop to a pulse.

tasks.title: Write the adjacency matrix of a directed 6-gene network, compute in-degree and out-degree for each node, and identify the master regulator
Count feed-forward loops and autoregulatory edges in a given 40-gene network and compare with the counts in 100 randomised copies
Simulate negative autoregulation against simple regulation after a step input and measure rise time and steady-state level of each circuit

schedule.title: Topology, centrality and robustness
schedule.exercise: Compute degree, betweenness and closeness for each node of a 10-node network by hand and rank the nodes by each measure.

tasks.title: Plot the degree distribution of a given interaction network on log axes and decide whether it follows a power law
Compute degree, betweenness and closeness for all proteins in a 150-node network and compare how the top 10 differ by measure
Remove nodes from a network by random order and by highest degree, track the largest connected component, and compare with a list of essential genes

schedule.title: Rate laws and gene expression models
schedule.exercise: Write the ODEs for a gene that is transcribed at a constant rate and degraded, solve for the steady state, and find the time to reach 90 percent of it.

tasks.title: Plot protein concentration over time for given production and degradation rates, and read off the steady state and half-life from the plot
Plot Hill functions for coefficients 1, 2 and 4, and fit the threshold and steepness that best match a given dose-response table
Simulate a two-step enzyme reaction with mass-action ODEs, compare with the Michaelis-Menten approximation, and report where the approximation breaks down

schedule.title: Switches, oscillators and stability
schedule.exercise: Find the fixed points of a two-gene mutual repression model, classify their stability, and sketch the phase plane with the nullclines.

tasks.title: Draw the phase plane of a two-variable gene model with nullclines and mark the fixed points it contains
Simulate the toggle switch from many starting points, show two stable states, and sweep an inducer to trace hysteresis
Simulate the repressilator, vary the Hill coefficient and degradation rate, and map the region of parameters where sustained oscillations appear

schedule.title: Noise and the stochastic simulation algorithm
schedule.exercise: For a birth-death model of mRNA with production rate k and decay rate g, write the reactions and propensities and find the mean and variance at steady state.

tasks.title: Step through five events of the stochastic simulation algorithm for a birth-death process, recording the random waiting time and reaction chosen each time
Implement the direct method for mRNA production and decay, run 200 trajectories, and compare the mean with the ODE solution
Simulate two identical genes in one cell and separate intrinsic from extrinsic noise by comparing their fluctuations over 500 simulated cells

schedule.title: Bursting, noise-induced switching and approximation
schedule.exercise: Explain why bursty expression gives a Fano factor above one, and decide for given molecule numbers whether an ODE model is a safe approximation.

tasks.title: Compute the Fano factor of simulated protein counts for steady and bursty promoters and compare the two histograms
Implement tau-leaping for a gene model, compare speed and accuracy with the exact method at three step sizes, and report the trade-off
Simulate the toggle switch stochastically, count how often noise flips the state at low and high copy numbers, and relate flips to the barrier height

schedule.title: Stoichiometry and flux balance analysis
schedule.exercise: Write the stoichiometric matrix of a five-reaction pathway, find its steady-state flux space, and set up the linear program that maximises one flux.

tasks.title: Build the stoichiometric matrix of a small 4-metabolite pathway and find which flux vectors satisfy S v = 0
Solve a flux balance problem on a 6-reaction network with uptake limits, report the optimal flux through the objective, and list the active constraints
Code flux balance analysis with a linear programming routine for a core metabolic model and verify it against a hand-solved small case

schedule.title: Growth, knockouts and genome-scale models
schedule.exercise: Predict whether a bacterium grows when each of five genes is removed, and explain which reactions make a gene essential on a minimal medium.

tasks.title: Knock out each reaction of a core model in turn, record the predicted growth rate, and list the essential reactions
Vary glucose and oxygen uptake over a grid, plot the predicted growth surface, and identify the switch between respiration and fermentation
Run flux variability analysis on a model with alternative routes, report which fluxes are fixed or flexible, and explain what the flexibility means

schedule.title: Boolean and logic models
schedule.exercise: Write the update rules of a 4-node Boolean network, list its state transitions under synchronous updating, and find its attractors.

tasks.title: Step a 4-node Boolean network from 4 starting states under synchronous updates and record each trajectory until it repeats
Enumerate all 256 states of an 8-gene Boolean network, find every attractor, and report the size of each basin of attraction
Encode a signalling pathway of 10 nodes from a given interaction list, knock out each node in turn, and rank candidate drug targets by effect on the output

schedule.title: Fitting models to data
schedule.exercise: Fit the decay rate in a one-variable ODE to noisy measurements by least squares, report the residuals, and say which parameters the data cannot determine.

tasks.title: Fit an exponential decay curve to 12 noisy time points by least squares and plot data, fit and residuals
Compute local sensitivities of the steady state of a gene model to each of five parameters and rank the parameters by influence
Fit a two-parameter model whose parameters are correlated, map the cost surface, and show a ridge where the parameters cannot be told apart

schedule.title: Optimisation, uncertainty and model choice
schedule.exercise: Compare two rival models of the same dataset using AIC, and describe how a bootstrap gives a confidence interval for a rate constant.

tasks.title: Run gradient descent on a two-parameter least-squares cost, plot the path across the contour map, and compare it with the exact minimum
Fit a one-step and a two-step activation model to the same time course and choose between them using AIC and BIC
Sample the posterior of a degradation rate with Metropolis steps, plot the chain, and compare the credible interval with a bootstrap interval

schedule.title: Model workflow and mini project
schedule.exercise: Write the model card for your mini project: question, assumptions, equations, parameters with units, data used, and how a reader could re-run it.

tasks.title: Add units and annotations to a given gene model and write it out in a structured exchange format so it can be re-run
Build a small host-parasite network model of the blood stage, simulate a drug that blocks one step, and report the predicted change in parasite load
Choose a small network, build the model, simulate it, fit it to a given dataset, and report fit quality, sensitivity and one prediction you can test
